key_insight: For controlled wake flows, more compact latent compression is not always better: POD produces smoother, easier-to-predict latent dynamics and more reliable long-horizon forecasts than nonlinear autoencoders.
engineering_relevance: For real-time flow control, especially model predictive control and reinforcement learning, choosing a representation that preserves forecast stability can matter more than maximizing compression.
method: Compare POD with convolutional autoencoders and two variational autoencoders for spatial compression.
Train Long Short-Term Memory predictors on latent coordinates for two 2D actuated wakes: a simplified truck wake and the fluidic pinball.
Evaluate reconstruction quality, latent-dynamics regularity, and long-horizon forecast robustness.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that CAEs give sharper short-term reconstructions and better compression, but their latent trajectories are more irregular, with faster forecast degradation and a higher chance of catastrophic divergence than POD-based ROMs.
watch_item: Highly compressed nonlinear latent spaces may look good in reconstruction tests yet become unstable or unreliable when extrapolated over longer control horizons.
paper_title: The balance between compactness and forecast accuracy of data-driven latent-space reduced-order models in controlled wake flows
